questions.stem: How is the relationship between Data Quality and Data Integrity described?
options: Data Quality is one component that supplements Data Integrity alongside other components
Data Quality and Data Integrity are two competing terms for the same idea
Data Integrity is one small component of Data Quality
Data Quality replaces Data Integrity in modern organisations
Data Quality and Data Integrity are unrelated disciplines
questions.explanation: The two are not different competing terms; Data Quality supplements Data Integrity, being one of its multiple components.

questions.stem: From which point of view did the term Data Integrity originally come?
questions.explanation: The term Data Integrity came from a security point of view, though it also arose from sharing data more effectively and easily, so it is more than just security.

questions.stem: Which four components of Data Integrity are listed?
options: Data Integration, Data Quality, Location Intelligence and Data Enrichment
questions.explanation: The Data Integrity components listed are Data Integration, Data Quality, Location Intelligence and Data Enrichment.

questions.stem: What is Interoperability, as used in the discussion of Data Integration?
options: The process of removing duplicate records from a dataset
The encryption of data while it moves between systems
The audit of results shared with regulatory bodies
The exchange of information between different systems
The addition of information that is not available in the source
questions.explanation: The exchange of information between different systems is called Interoperability.

questions.stem: Which approach is named as a major way to give uniqueness to entities coming from multiple sources?
questions.explanation: Master Data Management (MDM) is one of the major approaches for giving uniqueness to entities that come from multiple sources.

questions.stem: Which approaches are described as the best way to prove an organisation's Data Integrity?
questions.explanation: Data Lineage and Metadata Management are the best approaches to prove Data Integrity.

questions.stem: In the bank branch example of Location Intelligence, what decision might a decision-maker take on learning that customers travel from a location 10 km away?
options: Close the branch and merge it with a nearer one
Install an ATM near that location to offload cash withdrawal activities from the branch
Increase the marketing budget for that branch
Replace the branch's database with a graph database
Send the customers' data to an external audit team
questions.explanation: If customers in a branch come from a location 10 km away, the decision-maker can install an ATM near that location to offload cash withdrawal activities from the branch.

questions.stem: Which type of database is named as being used for Location Intelligence datasets?
options: Relational databases in third normal form
questions.explanation: For location intelligence datasets, Graph databases (a form of NoSQL database) are used.

questions.stem: What does Data Enrichment mean as a component of Data Integrity?
options: Encrypting data so that it cannot be read by intruders
Removing inaccurate records before loading data
Copying data from one system to another without change
Adding information to the target datastore that is not available from the source, such as comparing marketing expense with customer feedback on social media
Proving where data came from through lineage
questions.explanation: Data Enrichment means adding more information in the target datastore which is not available from the source, for example comparing marketing expense with customer feedback on social media.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a technique for achieving Data Integration?
questions.explanation: Techniques listed for data integration are ETL, ELT, CDC, Data Replication, Data Visualisation and Streaming Data Integration. Database normalisation is not among them.
